---
title: "comparing_income_methods"
output: html_document
---

```{r}
# Load required libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(readxl)
library(scales)
library(showtext)

# Ensure fonts are loaded
font_add_google("Open Sans", "Open Sans")
font_add_google("PT Serif", "Georgia") 
showtext_auto()

# 1. Load and sort the data
income_comp <- read_xlsx("../data/processed/median_income_comparison.xlsx") %>%
  rename(Original = original) %>%
  arrange(Original) %>%
  mutate(
    # Create a rank from 1 (poorest) to 51 (wealthiest)
    Rank = row_number(),
    
    # Split the 51 districts into 5 distinct groups
    Income_Tier = case_when(
      Rank <= 10 ~ "Tier 1: Lowest Income (Ranks 1-10)",
      Rank <= 20 ~ "Tier 2: Lower-Middle Income (Ranks 11-20)",
      Rank <= 30 ~ "Tier 3: Middle Income (Ranks 21-30)",
      Rank <= 40 ~ "Tier 4: Upper-Middle Income (Ranks 31-40)",
      Rank >  40 ~ "Tier 5: Highest Income (Ranks 41-51)"
    ),
    
    # Lock the CD factor levels in this sorted order
    councildist = factor(councildist, levels = councildist)
  )

# Pivot the data for plotting
income_long <- income_comp %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Original, PUMS, NYHC),
    names_to = "Method",
    values_to = "Income"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Method = factor(Method, levels = c("Original", "NYHC", "PUMS"),
                         labels = c("Our Method (CT Population-Weighted)", 
                                    "NYHC (Areal Overlap)", 
                                    "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)")))

# 2. Create a loop to generate and save 5 separate plots
tiers <- unique(income_long$Income_Tier)

for (i in seq_along(tiers)) {
  
  tier_name <- tiers[i]
  plot_data <- income_long %>% filter(Income_Tier == tier_name)
  
  p <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = Income, y = councildist)) +
    
    # Draw the horizontal line connecting the estimates
    geom_line(aes(group = councildist), color = "gray75", linewidth = 1.2) +
    
    # Plot the dots
    geom_point(aes(color = Method), size = 4.5, alpha = 0.9) +
    
    # Custom colors
    scale_color_manual(values = c(
      "Our Method (CT Population-Weighted)" = "#2f56a6", # Blue
      "NYHC (Areal Overlap)" = "#4f9560",                # Green
      "PUMS (Synthetic Downscaling)" = "#e91e63"         # Pink
    )) +
    
    # FIXING THE X-AXIS: 
    # By setting the limits from 30k to 180k for ALL plots, the scale remains 
    # perfectly consistent as you scroll through the 5 tiers.
    scale_x_continuous(
      labels = scales::dollar_format(), 
      limits = c(30000, 180000), 
      breaks = seq(30000, 180000, by = 25000)
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = "Comparing Income Aggregation Methods",
      subtitle = tier_name,
      x = "Estimated Median Household Income",
      y = "Council District"
    ) +
    
    # Clean Theme
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      text = element_text(family = "Open Sans"),
      plot.title = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 16, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(family = "Georgia", size = 13, margin = margin(b = 10), color = "#8744BC", face = "bold"),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.title = element_blank(),
      legend.text = element_text(size = 10),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), 
      panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 11, color = "black", face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold")
    )
  
  # Print plot to the RStudio Viewer
  print(p)
}
```
